# .github/AGENTS.md — CI-failure runbook

Read this file when a check fails, not before.

You are editing an enforcement instrument. Read the vendored `ENFORCEMENT.md` before this lands.

## Reproduce locally

```bash
pnpm check:ci         # everything reusable-checks.yml runs: check:static plus every package's tests
pnpm check:static     # the static-checks job alone (format, lint, typecheck, type tests, attw, build)
pnpm --filter <pkg> test --shard=<i>/<n>   # one shard of a test job
```

## Standing facts

- **Each CI lane owns its turbo cache key prefix** (`turbo-<os>-<lane>-<sha>`). actions/cache keys are immutable: lanes sharing a key race, and the faster lane's partial save silently drops the slower lane's entries.
- **Test jobs are planned from recorded timings.** The `plan` job reads the newest `test-timings-<profile>` artifact from main, or from any branch when main has none, and balances packages over the fewest free `ubuntu-latest` jobs whose loads fit 5 minutes (`scripts/tools/test-timings.ts`). Each job builds first, then runs its packages' tests one at a time (`turbo run test --concurrency=1`), so its wall time is the sum it was planned from and each recorded duration is uncontended. The test run keeps the builds in its graph, never `--only`, so each test key carries every dependency's build hash; the builds are cache hits after the build step. A package over 5 minutes runs as vitest shards. The `timings` job records every measured package into this run's `test-timings-<profile>` artifact, so the next run of the same profile re-packs automatically.
- **The reusable workflows are shared with other repositories.** Consumers call them pinned by commit SHA; their contract is [Calling the reusable workflows](#calling-the-reusable-workflows). Everything specific to this repository is in the callers' inputs (`ci.yml`, `commitlint.yml`, `nix.yml`) and in `.github/actions/checks-lane`, this repository's lane hook. To change this repository's steps, edit that action; to change the shape, edit the workflow and keep its inputs backward compatible for pinned callers.
- **The Mergify queue draft runs the full suite; an ordinary pull request stays fast** (SYS-1369, owner 2026-11-11). A draft on `mergify/merge-queue/*` runs the per-change suite (`profile: per-change`, packed test jobs, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), the flake outputs with the cross-system compare (`.github/workflows/nix.yml`, `nix / outputs match across systems`), and the storybook-gherkin browser suite when its paths change (`.github/workflows/storybook-gherkin-browser.yml`). `.github/actions/classify-diff/action.yml` forces `full` on a draft, so a docs-only change still runs it. A pull request runs the static, gritlint and layers lanes and the `affected` lane at `profile: local` (`.github/ci/pr-tests.ts`), and its plan schedules no packed test job (`.github/ci/no-tests-before-merge.ts`, which refuses a draft head). Main runs the same suite again after the merge (`push` to `main`).
- **Mutation runs on main only: diff-scoped on push, a clean full run weekly** (SYS-1417, owner 2026-11-13). `reusable-mutation.yml` is one job on the caller's `runs-on` (the workstation's one `[self-hosted, mutation]` runner): it refuses any event but push, schedule and dispatch, any ref but the default branch, and `tool: cargo-mutants` (not implemented). `scripts/tools/mutation.ts run` takes the caller's `packages` one after another. In `diff` mode each package's base is the newest first-parent ancestor whose latest `mutation/<pkg>` check concluded success or neutral; none within 200 commits bootstraps a full run. A package whose closure (`pnpm --filter ...[<base>]`) did not change posts success. Otherwise it builds the upstream workspace packages (`turbo run build --filter=./<dir>^...`), runs `stryker plan --max-shards 1` (`--since <base>`, or `--full`), and a diff planned over `budget-seconds` posts neutral (deferred to the weekly run; the base still advances). It prints `git status --porcelain --ignored` before `stryker run --plan --shard 1/1` and after any failure, merges with `stryker merge`, and writes `report.json` in the common report shape: tested, killed, survived, noCoverage, timedOut, deferred, kill rate killed / (valid - timedOut), and survivor fingerprints (a hash of package, path, mutator, enclosing top-level symbol, mutated text, replacement and rank; never a line number). Survivors post success: report-only, never red. A run with more than 5% of tested mutants timed out is invalid (host starvation) and posts cancelled, which does not advance the base. A plan, run, merge or build failure, an exit 2 included, posts failure and fails the job, so main is red and the conductor's main-CI wake fires. In `full` mode the check goes only on the tested commit; a crash also posts `mutation-health` failure on the branch head, which the base walk never reads. The incremental cache is restored in `diff` mode only; `.stryker-tmp` is removed in an `always()` step.
- **Exception to `pull-request-jobs-check-after-a-frozen-install`: the single-job `check` job plans.** With `single-job: true` the gate job classifies, lays the `.deps/` tarballs through the consumer-devshell step, runs the plan phase (the timing record and recent passes read from the artifact API, the turbo dry run, the planner) and then the lane, as steps of one job, so a pull request boots two runners instead of six. That is the point of the mode (owner, 2026-10-28: "We need to consolidate our CI so it uses less runners"), and the planner is read-only: it writes no cache entry and no record. `single-job-plan-guard` fails the job unless the plan is `[]`.
- **Mergify is the only merge queue; no workflow needs a `merge_group` trigger.** Mergify merges through the draft on `mergify/merge-queue/*` (SYS-1369; it never sends `merge_group`, and `ci.yml` no longer declares it). `.mergify.yml` `queue_conditions` are the cheap PR checks; `merge_conditions` are the draft's checks (`build · lint · typecheck · test / the gate (pnpm check:ci)`, `nix / outputs match across systems`, `abort on mid-run merge conflict`). They must stay different: equal conditions let Mergify test in place and skip the draft, so the full suite never runs.
- **Never re-trigger a release by hand.** `scripts/tools/plan-release.ts` derives the phase from repository state, so a killed release leaves untagged versions the next push re-plans. Tagging and GitHub Releases are idempotent — a version whose `<pkg>@vX.Y.Z` git tag already exists is skipped (`scripts/tools/cycle.ts`, `scripts/tools/tag-released-packages.ts`).
- **nix.systemfsoftware.com is the package registry for `@systemfsoftware` packages.** Producers push their package tarballs there from `main`, consumers take them through flake inputs, and nothing is published to npm. The release path writes a git tag and a GitHub Release per unreleased version — no npm token, no OIDC, no trusted publisher to configure.

## Calling the reusable workflows

Five workflows are callable from any repository: `reusable-checks.yml`, `reusable-mutation.yml`, `reusable-commitlint.yml`, `reusable-nix.yml` and `conflict-check.yml`. Call them pinned by commit SHA (`uses: systemfsoftware/systemfsoftware/.github/workflows/<file>@<sha>`). Every input is optional except `conflict-check`'s two; a caller writes no composite action of its own.

**Where tools and actions come from.** A reusable reaches this repository's actions through `$/.github/actions/<name>`, which resolves to the workflow's own commit, never the caller's `./`. Its Deno tools (`test-timings`, `mutation-job`, `classify-diff`) come from `$/.github/actions/sfs-tools`, which sparse-checks out `scripts/` at `job.workflow_repository`@`job.workflow_sha`. `$/` needs runner 2.336.0 or newer, so a self-hosted fleet must run at least that. A non-root `working-directory` checks out only that directory (except `reusable-nix.yml`, whose evaluator needs the whole tree's objects).

**Consumer prerequisites.** A pnpm workspace with a committed lockfile and a `packageManager` field. Checks: `turbo`, a `test` script per tested package, and a `build` task where one exists. Mutation: every mutated package has a `src/**/*.workflow.ts` file, a `"mutation": "stryker run"` script and no `mutation:*` variant, and a `stryker.config.*` that spreads `sharedConfig` from `@systemfsoftware/stryker-config` and sets no `mutate`; the plan job runs `pnpm exec stryker plan --full` in each such package, so Stryker must load there after an install with no build. The report job installs nothing, since `mutation-job report` merges every package's parts into the `mutation-report-<run number>` artifact (one `mutation.json` in mutation-testing-report-schema, keyed by repo-relative path, and a `summary.md`). Commitlint: `@commitlint/cli` and a commitlint config in the workspace root. Nix: a flake whose `packages.<system>` and `checks.<system>` are derivations.

**Consumer dev shell (checks, mutation, commitlint).** A consumer installs systemfsoftware packages through its producer flake inputs: its flake's default dev shell lays `.deps/<name>-<version>.tgz` from nix.systemfsoftware.com, the package registry for `@systemfsoftware` packages, and its `pnpm-lock.yaml` names each one as a `file:.deps/` entry. Each installing job runs `$/.github/actions/consumer-devshell` before its hook-or-built-in routing or install step. The action does nothing unless the lockfile names a `.deps/` tarball; otherwise it installs Nix only when the runner has none, runs `nix develop --command true` in `working-directory`, and fails unless `.deps/*.tgz` exists, so a lane hook's own install finds `.deps/` in place.

**Private flake inputs (checks, mutation, commitlint, nix).** Each takes an optional `sfs-fetch-token` secret: a GitHub token with read access to the private repositories the flake's inputs name. Pass it explicitly, as in `secrets: { sfs-fetch-token: ${{ secrets.SFS_FETCH_TOKEN }} }`; `secrets: inherit` cannot fill it, since a repository secret name holds no hyphen. In each job whose own steps run Nix (the consumer-devshell step of checks, mutation and commitlint, and every `build` job of nix), `$/.github/actions/sfs-fetch-auth` appends `access-tokens = github.com=<token>` to the runner user's Nix config before Nix runs and deletes that line in a final `if: always()` step; without the secret both steps only log a line. Only `github:` flake inputs use the token. Nix reads that line after `/etc/nix/nix.conf`, and a plain `access-tokens` replaces the whole setting, so in that job the token replaces the job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` and every other `access-tokens` entry for Nix's fetches. A caller-set `NIX_CONFIG` or `NIX_USER_CONF_FILES` takes precedence, and the token then has no effect. Every later step of the job can read the token, including flake code evaluated with `--impure` and nix's `extra-steps`, so never pass it on an event that checks out code you do not trust. The deletion is best effort: a job stopped by its `timeout-minutes` or by losing its runner never runs it, so pass the secret only to runners discarded after each job or used by one trust domain. A caller's `checks-lane` hook does not get it.

**Event policy.** On a pull request, checks and nix run only what the diff can affect: a diff inside the docs set (`docs/**`, root `*.md`, `**/AGENTS.md`, `**/CLAUDE.md`, or `docs-globs`) skips build, test and nix; the plan still runs, after the classifier and without a turbo dry run, and only lanes with a `docs-run` run. The built-in `docs` phase installs, so on a docs-only diff the consumer-devshell step runs only when the lockfile names a `.deps/` tarball, and a docs-only diff leaves the lockfile unchanged. A merge-queue draft (`mergify/merge-queue/*`) always runs everything (SYS-1369). Any other event, any path outside the set, or a diff that cannot be read runs everything. The test planner skips a package whose turbo hash a remote cache or a passed run already holds, and nix builds only outputs whose `drvPath` differs from the base commit's (one that fails to evaluate there builds). Mutation runs on push and `workflow_dispatch` only: its `guard` job fails a `pull_request` (the queue draft included) or `pull_request_target` event with `mutation-on-pull-request` before anything installs. Commitlint runs on pull requests only and skips Dependabot.

**Permissions the caller grants.** Checks: `contents: read`, `actions: read`. Mutation: `contents: read`, `actions: write` (the plan reads the record, the report deletes per-job artifacts). Commitlint, nix and conflict-check: `contents: read`. Checks takes the `turbo-api` and `turbo-token` secrets for a remote Turbo cache. Checks, mutation, commitlint and nix take the `sfs-fetch-token` secret for [private flake inputs](#calling-the-reusable-workflows).

**The lane hook (checks only).** A caller that has `.github/actions/checks-lane/action.yml` at the root of its checkout gets it run once per phase (`plan`, a lane's id, `test`, `test-after`, `timings`, `gate`, `docs`) with inputs `lane`, `job` and `profile`; the workflow output `lane-source` is `hook`. Without one, or under a non-root `working-directory`, every phase runs `$/.github/actions/builtin-lane` and `lane-source` is `built-in`; the non-root case says so in the summary with `hook-not-visible-working-directory`. In built-in mode a `timings` of `test-timings` means this workflow's own planner, and `dry-run` defaults to `<pnpm> exec turbo run test --dry=json` on pull requests.

**On failure.** Each failing job writes one reason code, the local reproduce command and the next action to its step summary, annotates with them, and uploads its captured logs as `failure-log-<job>-<attempt>`. The codes are a closed set (`$/.github/actions/failure-summary`): `merge-conflict`, `classify-failed`, `install-failed`, `tools-ref-missing` (sfs-tools got no workflow repository or commit, or could not fetch the tools at that commit), `plan-failed`, `hook-failed`, `lane-failed`, `build-failed`, `test-failed`, `timings-failed`, `gate-failed`, `commit-message-invalid`, `nix-eval-failed`, `nix-build-failed`, `outputs-differ-across-systems`, `compare-artifact-missing`, `mutation-on-pull-request`, `mutation-failed`, `mutation-merge-failed`, `devshell-failed` (the consumer-devshell step: `nix develop` failed, or its shellHook laid no `.deps/*.tgz`), `sfs-fetch-auth-failed` (sfs-fetch-auth could not write the `sfs-fetch-token` line to the runner user's Nix config; a failed deletion at the end of the job only annotates, since it runs after the summary step), `timed-out` (the job's `timeout-minutes` or a cancellation stopped a step; a summary step that runs on `failure() || cancelled()` reports it), and `unclassified` for a failure none of them names.

**This repository dogfoods them.** `ci.yml`, `commitlint.yml` and `nix.yml` are callers. The mutation reusable's callers are consumer repositories, younna-ai first; this repository's packages re-enroll once they run on the Nix Stryker package (SYS-1417).

### `reusable-checks.yml`

Outputs `lane-source` and `test-jobs` (the planned test jobs as JSON, each with its `packages`; `[]` when every package was skipped); secrets `turbo-api`, `turbo-token`, `sfs-fetch-token`. Inputs stay backward compatible for pinned callers: add, never rename or remove.

| Input                  | Default             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `working-directory`    | `.`                 | The pnpm workspace root, relative to the repository root. A non-root value checks out only that directory and always runs the built-in lanes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `profile`              | `per-change`        | Passed to the checks-lane action unchanged; systemfsoftware's conformance profile (`local` or `per-change`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `record`               | `test-timings`      | Name of the timing record artifact the plan reads and the timings job writes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `timings`              | `test-timings`      | Command that runs the test-timings planner (the flake's `test-timings`, or a deno invocation of the script). With the built-in lanes, `test-timings` is this workflow's own planner                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `runs-on`              | `["ubuntu-latest"]` | JSON label list for the plan, timings and gate jobs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `test-runs-on`         | empty               | JSON label list for the test jobs and any lint lane that names none; empty means `runs-on`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `lanes`                | `[]`                | JSON list of lint lanes: {"id", "name", "timeout-minutes", "run"?, "docs-run"?, "fetch-depth"?, "runs-on"?}; `run` is a command after the lane's action. On a docs-only pull request a lane with `docs-run` runs that command after the `docs` phase instead, and a lane without one is skipped                                                                                                                                                      |
| `target`               | `300`               | Planner --target, seconds of predicted work per job                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `max-jobs`             | `12`                | Planner --max-jobs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `max-seconds`          | `1800`              | Planner --max-seconds; keep it at or under the test job's timeout-minutes in seconds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `timeout-minutes`      | `30`                | Each test job's timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `plan-timeout-minutes` | `5`                 | The plan and timings jobs' timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `gate-name`            | `the gate`          | Name of the job that passes only when every other job passed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `gate-lane`            | `false`             | Check out and run the checks-lane action's `gate` phase after the gate's own check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `gate-timeout-minutes` | `2`                 | The gate job's timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `single-job`           | `false`             | One job for a run with one lane and no planned tests: the gate job classifies, lays the dev-shell tarballs, plans, runs the lane and gives the verdict as steps. A docs-only diff plans `[]`; fails if the plan schedules a test job                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `node-options`         | empty               | NODE_OPTIONS for the test jobs (a lint lane sets its own `node-options`); GitHub refuses it from $GITHUB_ENV                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `pnpm`                 | `pnpm`              | How the test steps invoke pnpm                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `test-flags`           | empty               | Extra flags on the packed jobs' `turbo run test`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `shard-flags`          | empty               | Extra flags on a shard job's vitest run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `persist-credentials`  | `true`              | actions/checkout persist-credentials                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `fetch-tags`           | `false`             | actions/checkout fetch-tags                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `dry-run`              | empty               | Command printing turbo's `--dry=json` for the test task without `--only` (e.g. `pnpm dlx turbo@2 run test --dry=json`), so each hash covers the task's dependencies as the test jobs' own keys do; the plan skips a package whose task is a remote cache hit, or which last passed whole on the same dry-run hash. Empty plans every package, except that the built-in lanes default it to `<pnpm> exec turbo run test --dry=json` on a pull request |
| `docs-globs`           | empty               | Newline- or comma-separated globs that replace the docs set (`docs/**`, root `*.md`, `**/AGENTS.md`, `**/CLAUDE.md`). A pull request that changes only docs skips the test and timings jobs and runs only lanes with a `docs-run`; the plan still runs                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `turbo-team`           | empty               | Remote Turbo cache team; empty leaves the remote cache off                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

### `reusable-mutation.yml`

Secret `sfs-fetch-token` (see [private flake inputs](#calling-the-reusable-workflows)). The caller grants `contents: read` and `checks: write`.

| Input             | Default                       | Meaning                                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tool`            | (required)                    | `stryker` or `cargo-mutants`; cargo-mutants fails at once                                 |
| `mode`            | (required)                    | `diff` on a push to main, `full` for the weekly clean run                                 |
| `packages`        | (required)                    | JSON array of package directories, run one after another                                  |
| `stryker`         | `""`                          | The Stryker Nix installable pinned to a release commit; required with `tool: stryker`     |
| `budget-seconds`  | `900`                         | A diff planned over this many seconds is deferred to the weekly run, with a neutral check |
| `timeout-minutes` | `180`                         | Timeout of the mutation job                                                               |
| `runs-on`         | `["self-hosted", "mutation"]` | JSON label list of the mutation job                                                       |

### `reusable-commitlint.yml`

Secret `sfs-fetch-token` (see [private flake inputs](#calling-the-reusable-workflows)).

| Input               | Default             | Meaning                                                                                                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `working-directory` | `.`                 | The pnpm workspace root that holds the commitlint config and `@commitlint/cli`, relative to the repository root |
| `runs-on`           | `["ubuntu-latest"]` | JSON label list for the job                                                                                     |

### `reusable-nix.yml`

Secret `sfs-fetch-token` (see [private flake inputs](#calling-the-reusable-workflows)).

| Input                    | Default                                                                                                              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `working-directory`      | `.`                                                                                                                  | The flake's directory, relative to the repository root                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `systems`                | `[{"system": "x86_64-linux", "runner": "ubuntu-latest"}, {"system": "aarch64-linux", "runner": "ubuntu-24.04-arm"}]` | JSON list of {"system", "runner"}: one build job per entry                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `extra-steps`            | `[]`                                                                                                                 | JSON list of {"name", "installable"?, "run"} run after the sweep, from the flake's directory; `{system}` in either string is the job's system. An entry with an `installable` (`.#<attr path>`) runs only when that derivation changed; one without always runs |
| `compare-across-systems` | empty                                                                                                                | An installable (`.#<attr path>`, `{system}` substituted) whose output every system builds on every non-docs-only run and must build byte-identical to the first system's; a system with no output fails `compare-artifact-missing`                              |
| `timeout-minutes`        | `60`                                                                                                                 | Timeout of each build job                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `docs-globs`             | empty                                                                                                                | Newline- or comma-separated globs that replace the default docs set; a pull request inside the set builds nothing                                                                                                                                               |
| `runs-on`                | `["ubuntu-latest"]`                                                                                                  | JSON label list for the classify and compare jobs                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

### `conflict-check.yml`

| Input      | Default  | Meaning                                            |
| ---------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `base_ref` | required | Name of the base branch the PR targets (e.g. main) |
| `head_sha` | required | SHA of the PR head commit (never the merge ref)    |

## Failure runbook

| Failure                     | Root cause                                                      | Remedy                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `api:check` fails           | Public API surface changed in a package with a committed golden | `pnpm --filter <pkg> api:update` and commit `etc/*.api.md`                                            |
| Git step exits 128          | Dirty workspace cascading from a prior step                     | Inspect the first failing step, not the git step                                                      |
| Log download gives HTTP 403 | The GitHub API refuses log download without push access         | Open `https://github.com/systemfsoftware/systemfsoftware/actions/runs/<run_id>` and read the step log |
